Your teacher tells you which lesson you're on. Practise a little every day: go through the steps below in order, and tick
each one when you've done it. The microphone lets the page hear your saxophone and tell you which notes it heard.

## Practice tips

- **Sing first.** If you can sing it, you can play it: the song and the patterns go in your ear (audiation) before your fingers.
- **Breathe before you play** every pattern, the way you do in class.
- **Short and often.** Fifteen minutes every day beats an hour once a week.
- **Don't look at the music at first.** Play by ear; the music is there for checking.
- **Ask:** if a fingering doesn't sound right, show your teacher next lesson.

## For the teacher

This follows the class sequence on [JRI Recorder, on Saxophone](/mlt/jri-sax.qmd) (Book One, Units 1–12), in concert B♭,
E♭, C minor and G minor. "Where we are in class" picks the section; the notes he knows are the ones introduced up to it. The
echo patterns use only those notes in the key practised now, starting on the resting tone and moving by step; rhythm patterns
are the class's sets chanted by the site's conversational chant (RhythmChant), in the song's meter or the other (divisions
from Unit 5B). Each lesson's songs are the new song and two reviews, plus songs from the JRI Recorder, Mullen and elementary
collections so that major and minor, duple and triple all come up; songs are moved into the class keys. Before the echo
patterns, the rhythm patterns and every song with the band, the page establishes tonality, meter or both in one of the ways
the MLT books describe (`apps/shared/mlt/establish.js`, picked at random by the teacher's weights). The saxophone notes
(holding it, embouchure, tone, tuning, care) are from [Saxophone](/lessons/saxophone.qmd). Progress is kept in the student's browser only.
